title: Assign Letter Grades with CASE WHEN
description:
Convert numeric scores into letter grades using a CASE expression.

**Table: students** — `id`, `name`, `score`

Grading scale:
- 90–100 → `'A'`
- 80–89 → `'B'`
- 70–79 → `'C'`
- 60–69 → `'D'`
- Below 60 → `'F'`

Return `name`, `score`, and `grade`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE students (id INT, name VARCHAR, score INT); INSERT INTO students VALUES (1,'Alice',95),(2,'Bob',82),(3,'Carol',77),(4,'Dave',63),(5,'Eve',91),(6,'Frank',54),(7,'Grace',88);
solution_sql: SELECT name, score, CASE WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'A' WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'B' WHEN score >= 70 THEN 'C' WHEN score >= 60 THEN 'D' ELSE 'F' END AS grade FROM students ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: All 7 students with grades: Alice=A, Bob=B, Carol=C, Dave=D, Eve=A, Frank=F, Grace=B

hints: CASE WHEN is evaluated top-to-bottom — the first matching condition wins.
ELSE catches any score that doesn't match any WHEN clause.
explanation: CASE WHEN checks conditions in order. Because conditions are checked top-down, a score of 95 matches score >= 90 first and gets 'A' — we don't need to write BETWEEN. Grades: Alice(95)=A, Bob(82)=B, Carol(77)=C, Dave(63)=D, Eve(91)=A, Frank(54)=F (ELSE), Grace(88)=B.
